html:
The Peace of Nicias was a treaty between Athens and Sparta signed in March 421 BCE. It ended the first ten years of the Peloponnesian War and was named after the Athenian general Nicias, who negotiated it.

The way had been opened in 422 BCE, when the leading hawks on both sides, Cleon of Athens and Brasidas of Sparta, were killed in the same battle at Amphipolis. Both cities were tired. The treaty was meant to last fifty years. Each side would hand back prisoners and the places it had taken, so Sparta got back the men captured at Pylos.

It never really worked. Several of Sparta's allies, among them Corinth and Thebes, refused to sign. Amphipolis was never handed back. Alcibiades built an alliance against Sparta that was beaten at Mantinea in 418 BCE. Then in 415 BCE Athens launched the Sicilian Expedition, and by 413 BCE the two powers were openly at war again.
sum: The Peace of Nicias was a treaty between Athens and Sparta signed in March 421 BCE. It ended the first ten years of the Peloponnesian War and was named after the Athenian general Nicias, who negotiated it.
